summary_en: This study compares stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) given after about 3 months of osimertinib with osimertinib alone, in non-small cell lung cancer that has spread to the brain. Osimertinib is taken by mouth, and SRS is given as a single dose or in several doses, with schedules that depend on the size of the brain lesion (for example, 18Gy x 1 or 21Gy x 1 for lesions under 20mm, and 9Gy x 3, 6Gy x 5, or 5Gy x 5 for lesions 20mm or larger); how long osimertinib is taken is not stated. The study measures quality of life using questionnaires, and this is a Phase 2 study.
summary_es: Este estudio compara la radiocirugía estereotáxica (SRS) administrada después de unos 3 meses de osimertinib con osimertinib solo, en cáncer de pulmón de células no pequeñas que se ha diseminado al cerebro. El osimertinib se toma por vía oral, y la SRS se administra en una sola dosis o en varias dosis, con esquemas que dependen del tamaño de la lesión cerebral (por ejemplo, 18Gy x 1 o 21Gy x 1 para lesiones menores de 20mm, y 9Gy x 3, 6Gy x 5 o 5Gy x 5 para lesiones de 20mm o más); no se indica por cuánto tiempo se toma el osimertinib. El estudio mide la calidad de vida mediante cuestionarios, y es un estudio de Fase 2.
who_for: Non-small cell lung cancer with an EGFR activating mutation, confirmed at the enrolling institution.
At least one intact brain metastasis visible on contrast MRI of the brain.
Not yet started TKI therapy, or started TKI no more than 3 months before enrollment.
For randomization: detectable brain lesions that are not growing and may be viable residual disease.
not_for: Evidence of leptomeningeal disease on MRI of the spine or lumbar puncture cytology.
Neurologic symptoms or a lesion in the brainstem, motor strip, or other eloquent area that needs immediate SRS.
Active blood cancer or a second solid tumor known to spread to the brain.
Pregnant, breastfeeding, or of childbearing potential without highly effective contraception.
